findings.title: Negative cursor offset passed to queryset slicing
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 OptimizedCursorPaginator allows attacker-controlled cursor.offset < 0 to be used directly as queryset[start_offset:stop] when enable_advanced_features is true. All other paginators reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and raise AssertionError, and the comment claiming Django handles it automatically is false. An attacker can supply a cursor like '0:-5:0' via the cursor query param to trigger a 500/DoS or unintended row windows, bypassing pagination bound checks.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator assumes numeric key but used with datetime ordering
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:839 OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns cursor.value as int. The audit-logs endpoint uses it with order_by='-datetime' where the key is a datetime. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError and the queryset filter comparing a datetime column to an int is type-wrong. Requesting organization_auditlogs with optimized_pagination=true will crash instead of paginating.

findings.title: BasePaginator allows negative offset for prev cursors
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 start_offset is max(0,offset) for forward cursors but raw offset for is_prev cursors, so queryset[offset:stop] can receive a negative start. Django raises AssertionError for negative slices, causing 500s on crafted prev cursors. The later trimming check len(results)==offset+limit+extra still uses the original negative offset while the query used start_offset, so page trimming is also inconsistent.

findings.title: SET to ZSET change breaks existing Redis keys
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 process_spans now uses ZADD and src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN and _load_segment_data uses ZSCAN, but existing keys were written as SETs with SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN. Redis enforces one type per key and returns WRONGTYPE on mismatch. During rollout or with leftover keys, inserts, merges, and loads will error, losing or stalling spans. No migration or dual-read handling is provided.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM corrupts scores on duplicates
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE option, so Redis defaults to SUM. Members are span payloads scored by end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload exists in both source sets due to retries, reprocessing, or overlapping merges, its timestamp is summed (e.g., doubled), corrupting ordering and causing zpopmin eviction to keep/drop the wrong spans.

findings.title: Missing end_timestamp_precise crashes consumer batch
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 process_batch does val['end_timestamp_precise'] with direct indexing. Previously Span did not require this field and old messages lack it. A single message without the field raises KeyError, failing the whole batch and, as a poison pill, repeatedly blocking progress and causing backlog/lag. It needs .get with validation or fallback.

findings.title: Redirect depth cut fragments deep traces
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 the redirect-following loop was cut from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces with parent chains deeper than 1000 will stop early without fully resolving set_span_id, leaving the segment split across multiple span-buf:s: keys that never merge, causing duplicate/incomplete flushed segments.

findings.title: Span-count guard removed, silent truncation without observability
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:150 max_segment_spans remains configured but _load_segment_data no longer checks len(payloads) against it or emits segment_span_count_exceeded/log. Oversized segments are now silently truncated at insert by zpopmin to 1000 lowest scores evicted with no metric or log. Operators lose visibility and oldest spans are silently dropped, changing the prior drop-entire-segment behavior to silent partial data loss.
